card.name: Comma after a noun before qualifier
card.fires_on: A comma right after a noun phrase about people, patients, pets or events, where an qualifying phrase follows. Typical follow-ons are primarily, usually, including, particularly or especially.

modes.label: Comma before primarily/usually
modes.description: Comma after a group or noun, ahead of an adverb that narrows where or who.
modes.example: An estimated 200–300 million people<<,>> primarily in Africa, South America and East

modes.label: Comma after patients or fatal events
modes.description: Comma after patients, infections, or deaths, before including, particularly or especially.
modes.example: Rarely, patients<<,>> particularly those who have severe obstructive coronary

card.writes: It promotes qualifying adverbs such as mostly, mainly, primarily, usually and typically for the next word.
card.plain: It marks a comma where the text is about to add a qualifier like 'mainly' or 'especially'.
